objective: Create the platform repository skeleton described by the P0.2 design of the guide repository: one workspace, the layout every later package lands in, the module registry, the seven dependency rules generated from it, the migration lint, a boundary suite that proves both fire, the charter, the continuity records and their schemas, and the CI skeleton. Revised three times after independent peer review: four blockers, then three, then two total fail-open holes and a class of coverage gap running through all three rounds.
completed_scope: One pnpm workspace with the top-level layout the P0.2 design draws
modules/modules.yaml registering all 30 candidate modules of the ARCH-001 capability map, plus platform-configuration from the P0.12 design
Four module packages, tenancy, identity-access, audit and platform-configuration, each with a public contract and a private internal half; every exported function throws
packages/contracts and packages/observability, which import no module; services/api, which imports contracts only
scripts/registry.mjs, a strict dependency-free reader that refuses a malformed registry with a line number

scripts/boundary-rules.mjs and scripts/generate-boundary-rules.mjs, generating .dependency-cruiser.cjs and tsconfig.paths.json from the registry, stamped with the registry SHA-256 and compared by --check

scripts/migration-lint.mjs enforcing M1 to M6, denying by default on an unmodelled DDL statement, and reading SQL through a SINGLE-PASS SCANNER rather than four independent regex passes. It refuses what it cannot represent: a quoted identifier carrying anything outside [A-Za-z0-9_], a non-ASCII character in an unquoted one, and a dollar-quoted body
The file walk refuses what it does not read: a non-directory under the migrations root, a non-.sql file under a module directory, and the .sql extension is matched case-insensitively

scripts/validate_continuity.py, fail-closed. Its authority reader errors on any line it cannot classify; statuses come from closed sets; expires_at is enforced against the record date; the state-registry relation is total in BOTH directions; badf/gates.yaml is validated and must agree with the state file; the two badf/lifecycle.yaml statements the acceptance check stands on are pinned; and a Work Package cannot enter ACCEPTED or CLOSED ahead of its acceptance grant

scripts/coverage-gate.mjs, which fails the build when a protection this repository NAMES is witnessed by no fixture. It derives the list from the code - the audit verb list, the domain stem list, the generated rule shapes - so adding one without a fixture fails rather than quietly widening the unwitnessed set
scripts/mutation-check.mjs, 30 mutations, including six for the round-three refusals; two mutations whose labels described something other than what they did are corrected
tests/boundaries with a fixture workspace and fixture migrations, one violation shape per fixture for every fixture added since round two; 11 new fixtures this round
tests/unit with 50 tests, 14 of them the round-three forgeries, each kept so the hole cannot reopen quietly
badf/ with five registries and three records; schemas/ with five JSON schemas
evidence/security-proof/negative-control-6.md: branch protection applied and the control observed, both halves, for the first time
.github/workflows/ci.yml running the same nine commands a developer runs

assumptions: ASSUMED: the modular monolith of ARCH-001 section 4.1, with the seven dependency rules and one schema per module. ADR-001 decides this and is DRAFT_REQUIRED.
ASSUMED: the candidate modules of the ARCH-001 capability map are the registry entries. Whether each is a bounded context, a subdomain or an aggregate is BIZTRUST-DOMAIN-001's decision.
ASSUMED: dependency-cruiser as the checker. The rules are generated, so a different checker consumes the same registry.
ASSUMED: the migration lint is a deterministic script under scripts/, per P0.2 open question 5. It is a text check over SQL and its blind spots are listed under declared_non_coverage.
ASSUMED: GitHub as the host, with the branch protection the guide charter describes. This is now observed rather than assumed.
blockers: BT-G0 is unrecorded. ARCH-001 is a draft, and FOUNDATION_SEQUENCE.md slice S01 needs five human review seats that are unfilled. No P0 epic may be implemented until an architecture authority records it.
ADR-001, ADR-004, ADR-005, ADR-010 and ADR-011 are all DRAFT_REQUIRED. The rules in this repository are the proposal of a design at IN_REVIEW.

NS-001 is half done. Branch protection is applied and negative control 6 is observed, but its other half - a named human holding the repository-administrator seat in badf/agents.yaml - is not, and that registry has no field capable of holding an occupant's name. An agent applied a setting on an operator's instruction; that is not a named human recording that they decided it.

Peer review has returned REVISION_REQUIRED three times. This round's findings came from two fresh-context AGENT reviewers, and neither is the independent human verifier the P0.2 design names. No re-review of this head has happened, and the reviewer decides whether a revision closes a finding.
authority_status: The scaffold was built under a direct operator instruction, recorded in badf/authority.yaml under granted.repository_scaffold. That is an operator instruction recorded by an agent; it is NOT the expiring implementation grant from a business authority seat that the P0.2 design requires. Every other authority in that file is NOT_GRANTED, wp_001_acceptance included. The registry is now parsed strictly, its statuses come from closed sets, its expiries are enforced, and it must agree key-for-key with the schema-pinned mirror in both directions. What this does NOT establish is that any record here was written by a human: a forgery that edits all three records consistently still passes, and the only mechanism that addresses it is the approval requirement now enforced on main. Pushing this branch and updating pull request #1 are inside tool_authority.may; pushing to main is not, and the attempt recorded as evidence was refused by the protection rather than by restraint.
next_action: Fill the repository administrator seat with a named human in badf/agents.yaml, and have that person record the branch protection decision. The protection itself is applied and negative control 6 is observed; what is missing is the record and the name, which no agent may write.
recovery: Read AGENTS.md, then badf/authority.yaml, then badf/current-state.json and badf/next-actions.json. The branch is motor/p0.2/repository-and-boundaries off 062a0f7c1b350e4af695978b238b28e323b7d0e0 on main, and pull request #1 tracks it. First safe command: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, then pnpm verify, which runs the nine checks above in order. All nine were observed at this head with the exit statuses recorded. If any fails, the tree has diverged from this checkpoint and the answer is RECOVERY_REQUIRED, not a fix. Do not run two agents against this working tree at once: the boundary suite and the mutation check both mutate tracked files and restore them, so concurrent runs corrupt each other's readings.
declared_non_coverage: THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST. A forgery that edits badf/authority.yaml, badf/current-state.json and the checkpoint CONSISTENTLY passes every check in this repository. Nothing here binds a record to a human identity, and no validator can close that. The mechanism that addresses it is the approval requirement on main, recorded under NS-001. Verified deliberately after this round's fixes, not assumed.

badf/skills.yaml and badf/agents.yaml are validated for existence, non-emptiness and a version line only. An agent can set record-a-gate and grant-authority to AVAILABLE, or flip may_be_an_agent to true on all four authority seats, and nothing objects. Only the two badf/lifecycle.yaml statements the acceptance check depends on are pinned; the rest of that file is in the same position.
badf/agents.yaml has no field capable of recording who holds a seat. Occupancy lives in a free-text note, so NS-001's acceptance cannot be recorded in the record it names.

No CODEOWNERS exists. badf/agents.yaml routes badf/authority.yaml to a human owner and verifier in prose, and every commit touching it so far has been agent-authored with nothing objecting. Now that main is protected, a CODEOWNERS file would make that routing a mechanism.

The checkpoint's baseline_commit, branch and files_changed are checked for agreement with badf/current-state.json but are NOT verified against git. A commit that does not exist, or a path that is not a file, still validates.

The migration lint is a text check over SQL, not a parser. Its scanner handles comments, literals, dollar-quoted bodies and quoted identifiers in one pass, and it refuses what it cannot represent; it still cannot see dynamic SQL built at runtime, or an extension that creates objects as a side effect.

Deny-by-default triggers on a statement OPENING with CREATE, ALTER or DROP. GRANT, REVOKE, COMMENT ON, SECURITY LABEL, IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA, SELECT ... INTO, CALL, COPY, MERGE, REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, LOCK, ANALYZE, VACUUM, REINDEX and CLUSTER are outside it. COPY and MERGE write rows across a schema boundary, which is the same act INSERT is modelled for; this is a KNOWN OPEN FINDING from round three, not merely a limit.

M4 and M5 fire only on the resolved verb CREATE TABLE. CREATE FOREIGN TABLE, ALTER ... RENAME TO, CREATE VIEW and CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW are outside both, so a P0 domain table can still be created as a foreign table or reached by renaming a neutral one. KNOWN OPEN FINDING from round three.
Cross-schema reads and structural coupling - SELECT ... FROM another schema, PARTITION OF, INHERITS - pass. KNOWN OPEN FINDING from round three.
REFERENCES <table> with no column list escapes M2, and psql meta-commands such as \i pass silently. KNOWN OPEN FINDINGS from round three.

Rules 5 and 5b have no apps/-side fixture, so an app other than the control plane importing a module's public-but-not-contract file is caught by nothing. The coverage gate checks rule SHAPES, not both arms of each shape, so it does not catch this. KNOWN OPEN FINDING from round three.
Fixture target monoculture: rules 3, 4, 6 and 7 can each be narrowed to the single fixture target they point at with the suite staying green.

The boundary suite and the mutation check MUTATE TRACKED FILES and restore them in a finally. A concurrent or interrupted run can leave a loosened rule in a tracked source file, so a recorded PASS is not reproducible by construction. Observed during this round when two reviewers ran against one working tree. KNOWN OPEN FINDING.
Negative control 6 is observed; every OTHER runtime control is not. Nothing runs: there is no server, no database and no configuration.
Rule 7's outbound host allow-list does not exist, and apps/ contains only a README, so rule 7 binds nothing outside the fixture.
The contract lint over openapi/ and events/. Both directories are reserved and empty; the rules are P0.8 and P0.9.
The observability tests. The baseline is P0.11.
The security proof suite over tests/security/. The BT-G1 matrix needs BT-G0 first.
No fixture proves the typecheck fails, so the compiler is an unwitnessed instrument.
CI runs one Verify job with sequential steps, not the independently required checks the design names, and there is no Build job. Two checks are required on main: Verify and Scope boundary.

The mutation check covers the dependency rules and the migration lint. It does NOT mutate the record validator, the registry reader, the module-package check or the coverage gate, so the checks that guard authority and coverage are themselves tested only by their own suites.
Rules 1 and 2 are generated per module; the fixture exercises one instance of each family, and the coverage gate deliberately asks for families rather than instances.
The design's control 7 says the boundary check's GENERATION step catches a package with no registry row. It does not; a separate script does.
